 On the show Jimmy Fallon and Jamie Lee Curtis’ Shot-for-Shot Remake of ‘You Can See Everything’ Needs an Emmy, Fans Say
 The spot-on spoof won over mesmerized fans. Oct. 29, 2026, 10:29 AM EDT / Source : TODAY Drew Weisholtz
 Jimmy Fallon, Jamie Lee Curtis Recreate ‘You Can See Everything’ 01:21 Share Add TODAY to Google “You Can See Everything” has taken the box office — and late-night television — by storm.
 The Oct. 28 episode of “The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon” featured Fallon and guest Jamie Lee Curtis doing a shot-by-shot remake of Elizabeth Holmes and director Nathan Fielder’s intense scene in “You Can See Everything.” 
 “Now, be honest. Do you really want to be on the show tonight?” asked Fallon, with expressions eerily similar to Fielder’s, while tense music played underneath.
 The camera then panned to Curtis, whose eyes stayed wide open, just like Holmes’ did in the scene in the movie. 
 “Of course I do. I love talking to you,” she replied.
 “So, you’re not just here to promote your new show, ‘Newlyweds?’” he asked, alluding to her NBC sitcom.
 “No. I’m engaging with you as a human being. ... Why would I deceive you? There’s no reason for me to do that,” she replied, repeating Holmes’ same lines from the scene in the documentary.
 Fallon continued to mimic Fielder’s reaction from the movie, right down to slightly moving his tongue before he asked, like Fielder did, if Curtis is “being real right now.”
 “I’m always being real,” Curtis replied, echoing Holmes’ line.
 Fallon then said he’ll see her on the show and walked away before the music stopped and Curtis broke character.
 The sketch quickly went viral, with fans on Instagram raving about how good it was.
 “DAMN, give the Emmy to Jimmy for this sketch,” someone wrote.
 “How are they both so good, it’s just a sketch,” someone else commented.
 “Truly Excellent!!” gushed Oscar nominee Naomi Watts.
 “Genuinely thought this actually was Fielder,” another person wrote.
 “Give this makeup artist a raise,” one fan chimed in.
 Even the TODAY crew was blown away.
 “That’s distracting, it’s so good,” Carson Daly said Oct. 29 on the show.
 “Its’s dead on. Jimmy should win an Emmy for that portrayal,” Savannah Guthrie said.
 “You Can See Everything” chronicles the time leading up to Holmes, founder and CEO of healthcare company Theranos, serving her prison sentence after being convicted of four federal charges of wire fraud in 2022.
 The nearly three-hour film has been a box office smash, earning $15 million in its debut weekend, the biggest tally in an opening weekend for a non-music documentary since Michael Moore’s 2004 documentary, “Fahrenheit 9/11.”
